content.content: WHEN focus moves onto a node by a means other than a pointer click on that node, the viewer shall centre the viewport on that node, leaving the zoom level unchanged. On an axis where the graph fits within the viewport, a centring move shall bring the focused node's centre to the viewport centre, and margin on that axis is permitted: the pan limits this viewer records do not hold a centring move back there. On an axis where the graph overflows the viewport, the graph shall keep covering the viewport, and the pan limits this viewer records shall bind that axis: a centring move is not carried past those limits there. This rule governs a centring move alone; the clamp this viewer records for a pan or a zoom is left as it is recorded. WHEN the user clicks a node with a pointer, the viewer shall not move the viewport. Neither rule reaches a change of the panel's own focus, nor a focus that ends with no node focused as when a graph reload removes the focused node; those shall not move the viewport. Centring is a viewport move and nothing else: keyboard traversal order and its wrap, the visible focus emphasis on the focused node, the zoom that keeps its rule of zooming about the viewport centre, and the selection and detail a click produces all remain as their own decisions set them.
content.rationale: Keyboard traversal forwards and backwards (ruqsmuxz, rwonulnq) can carry focus to a node that is off screen, so a focus that arrives at a node by a means other than a pointer click on it also brings that node to the centre of the viewport; the move translates the view and does not rescale it, so the zoom level is preserved and the rule pposortu records, that zooming happens about the viewport centre, still governs every zoom the viewer performs. Centring is neither a pan nor a zoom - a pan is what a drag does (srsnqppq) and a zoom is what a scroll or pinch does (kyokxuml) - so the clamp yymrxqsk records does not reach a centring move on its own terms, and the rule therefore settles for itself where, and on what condition, a recorded limit reaches one. The axis decides that condition, because the covering the limits protect is achievable on one kind of axis and not the other. On an axis where the graph fits inside the viewport, no pan of any extent can make the graph cover that axis, so holding a centring move back would surrender the whole point of centring - the focused node landing where the eye already is - in exchange for a covering that is unattainable; there the node's centre goes to the viewport centre and the margin left at the edge is accepted. On an axis where the graph overflows the viewport the covering is attainable and the recorded limits already say where the graph may stop, so a recorded limit binds a centring move there and the move is not carried past it: that is why the carve-out is drawn per axis rather than per move, and why centring on an overflowing axis gains no freedom this decision gives it. The rule adds nothing to those limits elsewhere: a pan and a zoom keep the clamp yymrxqsk records, on the same trigger and to the same extent, since centring neither excepts nor re-routes them. A pointer click is carved out because it is a selection gesture with its own outcome (ltrnmrsr: select the node and show its detail): clicking a node leaves the viewport where it is, so selection stays select-only and the click does not become a second way of moving the view. The boundary at pltovtuo is deliberate - a change in the panel's own focus is not focus arriving at a node, and a focus that ends with nothing focused, as when a reload removes the focused node, is not focus moving onto a node either - so both keep pan, zoom and selection exactly as that decision holds them. Centring is a viewport move only: it does not reorder or skip any step of traversal or its wrap, it does not change how the focus emphasis ozxnxzus specifies is shown, and it does not touch selection, so each of those stays in force with nothing overridden.
